claims.statement: The AgentKit directory is a Git submodule reference checkout, while the app build declares a remote versioned AgentKit dependency and records its resolved revision separately.

Repository guidance assigns the host-neutral loop, approvals, providers, MCP client and built-in tools to separately released AgentKit, while TermindRemoteInfrastructure registers host, SSH and SFTP tools and composes their presenters alongside runtime built-ins.

TermindMCPBridge translates newline-delimited stdio JSON-RPC to bearer-authenticated HTTP, retains session/protocol headers, forwards responses, and requests session deletion at EOF; desktop HTTP transport and MCP application tools remain separate owners.

TermindWidgets renders ActivityKit summaries and workspace links using WorkspaceActivitySupport source shared with TFI; the bounded payload contains session summaries but no credentials or terminal output, and app-native services own activity updates.

The three test targets separate shared, desktop and mobile checks; original-module synthetic V1/V14 stores preserve migration evidence, and the forwarding benchmark is a standalone executable independent of app/test hosting.
Repository scripts cover version/resource maintenance, remote fixtures/forwarding measurement, and screenshot/device-frame production, with Python tests for version and benchmark tooling.

LandingPage is a separate Astro build with English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese locale helpers, legacy zh redirects, shared components/layouts, and an explicit allowlist importing marketing device frames rather than copying them into public assets.

Marketing separates final locale/device App Store artwork from immutable source captures and reproducible device frames; Astro produces optimized image outputs from allowlisted frame imports, while Design/Brand retains the brand master and visual guidance.

Xcode project metadata controls build targets, schemes, embedding and package resolution, while scheduled/manual repository automation refreshes OpenWiki and opens a documentation pull request rather than serving app runtime behavior.

Cross-repository AgentKit changes require testing and releasing the separate package before updating Xcode's minimum version and resolved revision together; architecture tests reject app-local redefinitions of package-owned runtime types.

The MCP bridge defaults to a loopback URL, accepts URL/token from environment or command line, refuses invalid URL or missing token, skips malformed stdin, emits JSON-RPC errors for failed requests with IDs, and best-effort deletes its session at EOF.

The mobile Live Activity controller restores one active or stale activity and ends duplicates; it serializes updates and retirement, ends on empty workspace state, and requires explicit start intent and start permission before recreating a missing activity.

The standalone forwarding benchmark consumes fixture metadata and validates connection limits; the Python benchmark runner builds its dedicated Release scheme with pinned dependencies and collects metric records, while architecture tests ensure it is not an app dependency or test-host workload.

The V28 fixture is generated against the historical Persistence framework at 0dc173d4b1d190071d35bc66f80ebb767d8b950c; its generator records provenance and forbids regeneration against current models.

The app's AgentKit remote package reference requires versions starting at 0.18.1 up to the next major version, and the committed Package.resolved pin governs Xcode builds rather than the reference submodule or sibling working tree.
The TFM scheme tests both desktop and shared-framework targets; window-presenting macOS and mobile key-window suites require explicit opt-in, and mobile tests run against a simulator destination.

The Chinese-localization script checks normalization and JSON validity, then rejects missing or unfinished Simplified/Traditional Chinese translations and spacing errors in the two app string catalogs by default; it does not validate AgentKit's own catalog by default.

Xcode declares AgentKit and AgentKitScrubber as products of one remote AgentKit package; the core product is linked by both apps and TermindDomain, TermindApplication and TermindPersistence, while the Scrubber product is linked by desktop, TermindRemoteInfrastructure and desktop tests; this does not establish the remote manifest's internal dependency graph.
App builds should pass -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile to avoid implicitly resolving a newer dependency revision than the version recorded in Package.resolved.

The Mac marketing capture runner requires macOS 27, defaults to the workspace scene in all three locales and accepts scene/locale filters; it builds TFM tests with resolved packages, waits for a focused-key-window readiness marker from the capture test, validates image dimensions, and backs up previous captures before replacing them, aborting on failed readiness, test or dimension checks.

The mobile marketing runner builds TFI tests using resolved packages on an iOS 27 simulator, captures each selected device and locale using a capture-test handshake, and installs the new source images only after the test succeeds and its expected capture count matches.

LandingPage uses locked npm dependencies for local Astro development; its production npm build first runs Astro's check and then builds the site with optimized image transformations of allowlisted device frames.

The MCP bridge distinguishes modern metadata-driven requests, whose HTTP headers carry protocol version, method and optionally encoded name without a session ID, from legacy requests that retain an assigned session ID and negotiated protocol version for subsequent calls and EOF cleanup.
The bridge's executable-level loopback check covers modern and legacy request headers, JSON-RPC error passthrough, and legacy session deletion.

The standalone forwarding benchmark waits for its SSH connection pool before measuring forwarding workloads across local, remote, dynamic, jump-host, streaming, and mixed modes; it prints structured FORWARDING_METRIC records and disconnects after success or failure.

The forwarding benchmark script builds the dedicated Release scheme with resolved Swift package versions, repeats runs at selected connection limits, and rejects successful executions that produce no metrics.

The libssh2-spm and libghostty-spm submodule checkouts do not supply Xcode's app build: the project references the remote libssh2 package at exact version 2.0.3-termind-4 and the remote Ghostty fork with an up-to-next-major version requirement from 2.2.2026100303, both captured in Package.resolved; Ghostty fork changes require updating the gitlink and both project and resolution records together.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests enforces ownership through source-level checks on app and framework imports and declarations, including a desktop-tree check against shadowing AgentKit runtime types and a guard that the forwarding benchmark remains independent of app targets and test hosting; these guards are not a benchmark workload.

Public website comparison and pricing pages share competitor data and Termind features in src/lib/comparisons plus centralized prices in src/lib/pricing.ts across three locales; legacy zh routes redirect.
